To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of 2-CFU cutoffs on Bacteriology Media Inc. BHI-V4/ BHI-V3 biplate agar for VISA and h/VISA screening, respectively, is a simple and reliable method that is consistent with PAP-AUC gold standard confirmation.
2 CFU on BHI-V 4 and 2 CFU or 16 CFU on BBI-V3 best approximate gold standard confirmation for VISA and h/VISA, respectively, with little overlap in samples with intermediate PAP-AUC values.

the use of vancomycin-supplemented brain heart infusion (BHI) agars for screening vancomycinnintermediately susceptible Staph. aureus (VSA) and heteroresistent (hVSA) phenotypes is feasible, and that 2 CFU on BHI-VS agar is the most appropriate cutoff for screening for VSA and hVSA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the screening of intermediately susceptible and heteroresistant Staph. aureus.
the development of a novel method to screen for vancomycin intermediately susceptible and vancomycin-heteroresistant phenotypes of methicillin-resistant S. aureus.

the development and standardization of growth cutoffs on BVI-V3 and BHI-V4 plates for the screening of VISA and h-VISA, respectively, and their application to manufacturer-made BHI biplates for simultaneous screening of VISA/hVSA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of 2-CFU cutoffs on BBI-V4 and BBI-V3 agar biplates is recommended for screening VISA and h-VISA phenotypes, respectively.
the proposed 2-CFU cutoffs on vancomycin-supplemented BHI agars best approximate VISA/hVSA gold standard confirmation with minimal overlap in isolates with borderline PAP AUC.
BHI-V4 plates with a cutoff of 3 CFU and BHI-V4 with a cutoff of <3 CFU are the best for screening for VISA and h-VISA, respectively, in the absence of PAP-AUC testing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of vancomycin supplemented brain-heart infusion agar biplates (BHI-V) is a useful method for detecting vancomycin intermediate Staphylococcal aureus (VSA) and vancomycin heteroresistant Staph aureus (hVSA) in clinical isolates.

we have defined the growth cutoffs that best approximate VISA (2 CFU) and hVISA (16 CFU) phenotypes, and we have demonstrated that manufacturer-made BHI agar supplemented with vancomycins 3 and 4 mg/liter can be used for simultaneous VISA/hVSA screening with a 2-CF/droplet cutoff.
we have developed a new screening method for hVISA and VISA.
The main takeaway from our work is that

BHI-V4 plates with a 2-CFUs/droplet cutoff are highly sensitive for VISA screening and BHI-V4/V3 biplates with a 2/16-CFUs/droplet cutoff are highly sensitive and specific for hVISA and VISA screening, respectively.
BHI-V4 agar plates can be used as a screening test for vancomycin-intermediately susceptible S. aureus, but a BHI-V4 plate with 2 CFU per droplet should be used.
we have established growth interpretation criteria for screening for intermediately susceptible and heteroresistant vancomycin Staphylococcal aureus based on a gold standard method of confirmation.
